_site_id_is_SHARED: SAME site as alpine_village_01. This is the interior view of the place that concept shows from outside. Build the site once; solve both cameras.
_read_by: Claude, 2026-08-29, multimodal read plus scripts/analyse_concept.py. Reading of record: _verify/20260829_concepts/READING.md.
_what_this_concept_is: INSIDE THE VILLAGE. Street level on a dirt track, buildings framing left and right, looking along the track at the church with the peak beyond. This is the DETAIL concept -- it is where the material and clutter requirements are legible.

features.shape: asymmetric horn, steep left face, long right shoulder -- THE SAME PEAK AS CONCEPT 01
features._cross_check: the peak sits near the centre line in both concepts. Once both cameras are solved, the village-to-peak vector must be consistent. That consistency is the cheapest available test that the site layout is right.

features._what: dirt track running away from camera through the village, curving right past the church. Patches of cobble near the buildings.
a shallow rivulet crossing the foreground left of centre, rounded river stones along and in it
the ground rises gently away from camera toward the church

items.form: rough stone ground floor, heavy squared-log or plank upper storey, wide shingled roof with deep eaves, stone chimney, upper balcony with turned railing on the right-hand one
items._these_are_the_FRAMING_buildings: one left, one right, at the frame edges. They define the street corridor and they are the closest, most legible architecture in either concept -- so they set the material bar.

items._silhouette_plausible_cm: DERIVED FROM GEOMETRY, not chosen. Walls are 400 cm (2 storeys x the ruled 2.00 m kit wall course). An alpine roof over the 8 m short span runs 30-45 degrees, giving 231-400 cm of roof and a 631-800 cm silhouette; the band is widened slightly to 620-820. THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS THE DEFECT THIS WEEK: 536.5 cm implies a 136.5 cm roof, an 18.8 degree pitch, far too shallow for a shingled roof with the deep overhang both concepts describe -- and 536.5 was exactly what the buried kit roof produced. The measured correct value, 738.0, is a 40 degree pitch and sits comfortably inside.

items.form: cream plastered walls; ornate painted or carved panel in an arched surround over the entrance; pointed arched windows; covered porch on posts with its own shingled roof; belfry stage with arched openings; WEATHERED COPPER ONION DOME, dark red-brown, with a finial above
items._the_most_detailed_object_in_either_imag: and the one thing no current library asset can approximate. Phase D candidate.
items._height_class_superseded: was 4. RULED 2026-08-30: the reader saw a nave AND a tower and flattened them into one number, which is why this recipe contradicted its own prose (1.5x) with its height_class (2x). A church is not the average of its nave and its spire. Replaced by parts[]; this value is inert and kept only so the history reads.

parts._source: the concept's own prose: 'roughly half again the height of the houses'
what made height_class read 2+. CORROBORATED by measurement: the Phase B loop built the church at 2.24-2.61x the chalet silhouette, and the operator ruled that reading stands as the SPIRE.

items._what: an arched passage between buildings right of the church

focal_anchor._why: the composition funnels to it -- track, buildings and the peak all sit on the centre line through the tower. It is the subject of this concept, not merely present in it.

classes._what: neat stacked split logs -- deep in the left undercroft, beside the church, and on the right. At least four distinct piles.
classes._why_this_matters: it is the single most repeated object in the concept and it is what makes the place read as INHABITED rather than merely built. Cheap, high value.

classes._what: small white and red flowers through the foreground grass
small wooden cart with painted red detail, left frame edge

sun._elevation: INFERRED. Softer and more diffuse than concept 01 -- consistent with the same low sun seen through heavier morning haze rather than a different time.
sun._azimuth: REFUSED as a number, same reasoning as concept 01. Image-space shadow bearing measured 175.2 deg at coherence 0.181 -- close to isotropic, so it is not evidence.
sun._colour: MEASURED, top 15% of luma on the ground band. R-B +0.183 -- WARMER than concept 01, consistent with more atmosphere between sun and subject.

shadow._colour: MEASURED. R-B +0.004, essentially NEUTRAL -- not the cool blue of concept 01. The haze is filling shadows here.

haze._status: MEASURED CLEANLY HERE. This composition has near ground at the bottom and hazed peak at the top, so image height is a good depth proxy.
haze._ratio: the far field retains ~58% of near-field saturation. This is a TUNING TARGET for the aerial-perspective block -- the project's fog has been 'applied and rendering, never tuned' since 2026-08-06, and this is the first number to tune it against.

time_of_day.label: early_morning
time_of_day.evidence: LIT LANTERNS on the buildings, heavy low mist, soft diffuse light. The lanterns are the strongest single witness -- they are on because it is still dim.

artificial._note: a time-of-day witness as much as a light source

camera.position_hint: standing on the dirt track inside the village, buildings close on both sides, church ahead on the centre line
camera._fov: both flanking buildings are in frame at close range while the peak still reads at distance -- wider than concept 01
camera.framing_device: pine branches intruding at top left

_schema_1_2: 1.2 adds plausible_cm bands on ratio-scored heights. A ratio check cannot detect an error in the quantity it is a ratio OF -- both terms move together and the quotient stays right, which is how ruling 1 was scored against a chalet whose roof was buried 201.49 cm in its walls. A band is an ABSOLUTE check and is the only kind that can catch that.
